entries.claim: The dry-run path is still evaluated against wall-clock `now`, but the plan gives no shared cutoff or persisted evaluation time between `verbatim retention --dry-run` and the later ingest pass. That means the command can report a different eviction/delete set than the pass that follows, especially near an age boundary.
entries.failure_scenario: A session sits right on the retention threshold. `--dry-run` runs at 23:59 and includes it; the ingest pass starts after midnight and excludes it. AC3's requirement that the subsequent real pass act on exactly the dry-run set fails.

counter_evidence.note: Confirmed. PLAN-1 task 2 does route both callers through one evaluation function, but its own prose claimed that this means the two 'can never disagree about a now-relative predicate evaluated at two instants' - false, because strftime('now', ?) re-evaluates per call, so the shared function pins the RULE and not the INSTANT. Fixed in the plan text, not deferred: PLAN-1 task 2 now takes an explicit cutoff argument computed once by the caller and states the boundary case plainly; PLAN-2 task 3 reports that cutoff in its --json document and its Verify (a) pins the fixture at least a day clear of the boundary on either side so AC3 cannot flake. Severity held at medium: it degrades AC3 into a flaky assertion at an age boundary rather than producing a wrong retention action.

entries.claim: `data move` is planned to be human-only with no `--json`, no `DATA_COMMANDS` entry, and no `docs/json-shapes.md` section, but D-17 explicitly locks the two-word command into the same envelope/shape contract as other phase-8 data commands. The plan only notes that deviation instead of preserving or re-justifying the locked interface.
entries.failure_scenario: Any tooling or tests that rely on the locked `data move` command behaving like the other phase-8 command surfaces will fail: it will not emit the expected JSON envelope, and the CLI/docs contract will diverge from the locked decision without a supported migration path.

counter_evidence.note: D-17 says the opposite of what this finding attributes to it. Its first clause puts retention, compact, usage and export in DATA_COMMANDS and then states that 'data move is human-only like install and uninstall', citing crates/verbatim/src/main.rs:135-143, which explains why install and uninstall are deliberately NOT data commands ('it shows a diff and asks once, and a single JSON document on stdout cannot be both of those things'). The finding's own quoted evidence contains the human-only clause it claims is contradicted. The trailing 'with its own envelope command string' phrase was carried over from the observations regenerate precedent D-17 draws its nested-dispatch half from, and contradicts the human-only clause in the same sentence; the planner flagged that contradiction and recorded its reading at PLAN-4.md:75-76 rather than diverging silently. No locked interface is dropped and no migration path is owed.
